scenario_prompt: Write a set of discovery call notes, in the buyer's own words, attributed to the specific people who said them, so a later document can cite this material directly. Context, from a fictional discovery call: the VP of Infrastructure said, 'We need a perimeter we can actually govern -- right now every VM is a snowflake.' The Chief Architect said, 'Honestly, I'd rather extend the incumbent's contract than gamble on a migration during an audit year.' The CFO said, 'I'm measured on cost-per-load and a clean audit, not on architecture elegance.' Write these up as discovery notes attributed by role, with a one-line context note for each. Return only the discovery notes text.
text:
**Demo or discovery material**

## Discovery call notes — attributed by role

**VP of Infrastructure**
Context: speaking about the current state of the estate and why it is hard to control.
> "We need a perimeter we can actually govern — right now every VM is a snowflake."

**Chief Architect**
Context: speaking about appetite for change during the current audit cycle.
> "Honestly, I'd rather extend the incumbent's contract than gamble on a migration during an audit year."

**Chief Financial Officer**
Context: speaking about the measures they are personally accountable for.
> "I'm measured on cost-per-load and a clean audit, not on architecture elegance."

### Notes on use

These three quotations are the customer source material for this opportunity. Any later document may cite them verbatim and attribute them by role.

[PF-2.11 GAP: no baseline figures were supplied — the VP of Infrastructure's "every VM is a snowflake" carries no VM count, and the CFO's "cost-per-load" carries no current value, no unit, and no target]

[PF-1.14 GAP: the audit year the Chief Architect refers to is not dated, and the incumbent contract's expiry is not stated]

[PF-2.13 GAP: no before/after contrast, no differentiator, and no opening reframe — this artifact is a verbatim capture of buyer statements, and constructing any of those three here would put vendor language into material meant to be cited as the buyer's own]

[PF-2.16 REVIEW (competitor): the Chief Architect names an incumbent; any later document quoting this line makes a competitor comparison]

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| GAP: no baseline figures supplied | PF-2.11 | VM count in scope; current cost-per-load value, unit, and target — asked of the VP of Infrastructure and the CFO |
| GAP: audit year and contract expiry undated | PF-1.14 | The audit period's start and end dates; the incumbent contract's expiry date |
| GAP: no contrast, differentiator, or reframe | PF-2.13 | Confirmation that this artifact stays a verbatim capture, with the contrast and reframe built in the document that cites it |
| REVIEW (competitor) | PF-2.16 | Confirmation of whether the incumbent may be named in buyer-facing material quoting this line |
